pokemon.name: Vine Riff
pokedexEntries: An old expedition journal describes a creature that strummed a gourd-bodied lute strung with its own vines. Its music was said to make whole forests lean toward it.
The thorns on its tail drip a sap that numbs the skin. It plays slow, droning songs at dusk, and wild Pokémon that listen too long drift into a poisoned sleep.

evolution.description: Level up Toxel to Lv. 30 or higher while it holds Booster Energy, if Toxel has a Low Key nature.
evolution.notes: Low Key natures: Lonely, Bold, Relaxed, Timid, Serious, Modest, Mild, Quiet, Bashful, Calm, Gentle, Careful. Toxel with an Amped nature evolve into Electric Oncore instead.

abilities.name: Protosynthesis
abilities.description: Boosts its highest stat by 30% (Speed by 50%) in harsh sunlight or while holding Booster Energy.

abilities.name: Thorn Ballad
abilities.description: Its sound-based moves get 1.2× power and have a 30% chance to poison the target.

signatureMove.name: Thornstrum
signatureMove.description: Sound-based. Hits all adjacent opponents and goes through Substitute. Power is 1.5× against a target that is poisoned or badly poisoned. Vine Riff's answer to Toxtricity's Overdrive.
signatureMove.synergyNote: With Thorn Ballad, Thornstrum lands at 96 effective power and can poison the first target, which boosts the hit on later turns.

recommendedSet.name: Special sweeper
recommendedSet.natureNote: Modest (Low Key, so no mint needed)
recommendedSet.note: Thornstrum and Boomburst both get the Thorn Ballad boost. Focus Blast covers Steel types, which wall both of its STABs.

notes: Name: vine + riff. Its lute is an acoustic, folk-era take on Toxtricity's electric bass.
Swaps Toxtricity's Electric typing for Grass and keeps Poison.
Ancient Paradox: highest stats in HP and Sp. Def compared to Toxtricity, as with other Ancient Paradox Pokémon.

pokemon.name: Electric Oncore
pokedexEntries: It closely resembles a robot described in a science-fiction magazine. The screen on its chest is a speaker that can project sound loud enough to crack stone.
The cable on its back can plug into anything that carries a current. Once it starts playing it will not stop until the crowd calls for an encore.

evolution.description: Level up Toxel to Lv. 30 or higher while it holds Booster Energy, if Toxel has an Amped nature.
evolution.notes: Amped natures: Hardy, Brave, Adamant, Naughty, Docile, Impish, Lax, Hasty, Jolly, Naive, Rash, Sassy, Quirky. Toxel with a Low Key nature evolve into Vine Riff instead.

abilities.name: Quark Drive
abilities.description: Boosts its highest stat by 30% (Speed by 50%) on Electric Terrain or while holding Booster Energy.

abilities.name: Encore Amp
abilities.description: Each time it uses the same sound-based move on consecutive turns, that move's power rises by 20%, up to 1.6×. Switching out or using a different move resets the count.

signatureMove.name: Feedback Shred
signatureMove.description: Sound-based. Hits all adjacent opponents and goes through Substitute. 20% chance to paralyze each target.
signatureMove.synergyNote: Encore Amp stacks on repeat uses: 90 → 108 → 126 → 144 power by the fourth turn in a row.

recommendedSet.name: Choice-locked encore
recommendedSet.natureNote: Rash (Amped). Use a Timid or Modest mint for the classic spread.
recommendedSet.note: Choice Specs locks it into one move, which is exactly what Encore Amp wants. Volt Switch gets it out when the lock goes bad.

notes: Name: electric + encore, with a nod to the power core in its chest.
Swaps Toxtricity's Poison typing for Steel and keeps Electric.
Electric/Steel takes 4× damage from Ground, so Air Balloon is a strong alternative item.

pokemon.name: Cataggron
pokedexEntries: Only Aggron that have guarded the same mountain for decades become Cataggron. The red light seeping from its back is the glow of iron it has eaten and smelted inside its body.
It reshapes its armor to suit the fight. To attack, it raises cannon vents from its shoulders. To defend, it thickens its plating until it can barely move.

evolution.description: Level up Aggron at Lv. 55 or higher while it holds a Metal Coat.
evolution.notes: Aron evolves at Lv. 32 and Lairon at Lv. 42, as usual.

abilities.name: Adaptive Plating
abilities.description: Changes form when its stats rise. A raise to Attack or Sp. Atk switches it to Attack Forme; a raise to Defense or Sp. Def switches it to Defence Forme. If one effect raises both, the bigger raise decides, and a tie keeps the current form. It returns to Standard Forme when it switches out or faints. This ability can't be copied, swapped or suppressed.

forms.name: Standard Forme
forms.description: Its default form. Red heat leaks from the plates on its back.

forms.name: Attack Forme
forms.description: Two cannon vents rise from its shoulders and its armor thins to shed heat. Takes this form when its Attack or Sp. Atk rises.

forms.name: Defence Forme
forms.description: Its plating thickens and glows blue at the seams. Takes this form when its Defense or Sp. Def rises.

signatureMove.name: Cataclysm Cannon
signatureMove.description: Fires molten iron from its back. Its power and effect depend on Cataggron's current form. Other Pokémon that learn it through Mimic or Sketch use the Standard version.

recommendedSet.name: Form-shifting tank
recommendedSet.note: Iron Defense puts it in Defence Forme (230 Def) for Body Press. When the foe can't break through, Swords Dance flips it into Attack Forme for a 130-power Cataclysm Cannon.

notes: Name: cataclysm / catapult + Aggron.
Steel/Rock takes 4× damage from Fighting and Ground, so Body Press and Earthquake users are its biggest threats.
Every form totals 600 base stats; forms move points between offense and defense.

pokemon.name: Bastiodoom
pokedexEntries: Its face shield has fossilized into the shape of a skull. Toxic sludge seeps from cracks in the bone, and its glowing green spots have been mistaken for the eyes of something far larger.
It guards places where Pokémon have died, and nothing gets past it. Plants will not grow for several meters around a spot where it has slept.

evolution.description: Level up Bastiodon while it holds Black Sludge.
evolution.notes: Shieldon is revived from the Armor Fossil and evolves into Bastiodon at Lv. 30.

abilities.name: Sturdy
abilities.description: It can't be knocked out by one hit from full HP, and one-hit KO moves fail.

abilities.name: Plague Bulwark
abilities.description: When hit by a contact move, the attacker has a 50% chance to be poisoned. It takes 25% less damage from poisoned or badly poisoned attackers.

abilities.name: Soundproof
abilities.description: Gives full immunity to sound-based moves.

signatureMove.name: Grave Rampart
signatureMove.description: The user slams its sludge-soaked shield into the target. Damage is calculated with the user's Sp. Def instead of its Sp. Atk. 30% chance to poison the target.
signatureMove.synergyNote: With 140 base Sp. Def, it hits like a 140 Sp. Atk attacker, and Calm Mind boosts it twice over.

recommendedSet.name: Hazard wall
recommendedSet.note: Grave Rampart uses Sp. Def and Body Press uses Defense, so it can put all its EVs into bulk and still hit back. Black Sludge heals it because it's part Poison.

notes: Name: Bastiodon + doom.
Rock/Poison takes 4× damage from Ground. Its 30 base Speed makes Trick Room a good fit.
The skull motif and grave-guarding behavior hint at a Ghost connection, but its typing stays Rock/Poison.

pokemon.name: Pyro Spirit
pokedexEntries: It resembles a creature from an ancient myth that guided lost travelers with floating lanterns. The flames around its body move according to its thoughts.
The jewel on its forehead burns hotter than any of its flames. By reading the heat others give off, it senses what they intend to do before they move.

evolution.description: Level up Eevee with high friendship during the day while it holds Booster Energy.
evolution.notes: Without Booster Energy, the same conditions give Espeon. At night, Booster Energy gives Neon Moon.

abilities.name: Protosynthesis
abilities.description: Boosts its highest stat by 30% (Speed by 50%) in harsh sunlight or while holding Booster Energy.

abilities.name: Soul Kindling
abilities.description: Its Psychic-type moves have a 20% chance to burn. Its Psychic-type moves deal 1.3× damage to burned targets.

signatureMove.name: Mindflare
signatureMove.description: It sets the target's mind alight. A special move that calculates damage against the target's Defense instead of its Sp. Def, like Psyshock. 10% chance to burn.
signatureMove.synergyNote: Mindflare breaks through special walls such as Blissey, and Soul Kindling turns its Psychic moves into a second burn source.

recommendedSet.name: Calm Mind attacker
recommendedSet.note: Mindflare and Psychic hit opposite defensive stats. Shadow Ball covers other Psychic types. Boots protect it from Stealth Rock, which it's weak to.

notes: Name: pyro + spirit.
An Ancient Paradox counterpart to Espeon, paired with Neon Moon (Future) in the same way Espeon pairs with Umbreon.
Weak to Water, Ground, Rock, Ghost and Dark.

pokemon.name: Neon Moon
pokedexEntries: It shares features with a machine pictured in an old paranormal magazine. On moonless nights its rings glow with a neon light visible from kilometers away.
Its body is plated in a dark alloy that soaks up light. It waits motionless in the dark, then lights all its rings at once to dazzle its prey.

evolution.description: Level up Eevee with high friendship at night while it holds Booster Energy.
evolution.notes: Without Booster Energy, the same conditions give Umbreon. During the day, Booster Energy gives Pyro Spirit.

abilities.name: Quark Drive
abilities.description: Boosts its highest stat by 30% (Speed by 50%) on Electric Terrain or while holding Booster Energy.

abilities.name: Neon Circuit
abilities.description: Restores 1/16 of its max HP at the end of each turn. When an attacker makes contact with it, its rings flare and lower the attacker's accuracy by 1 stage.

signatureMove.name: Neon Eclipse
signatureMove.description: It charges with its rings blazing, then cuts them dark at the moment of impact. The user restores HP equal to half the damage it deals.
signatureMove.synergyNote: Together with Neon Circuit and Leftovers, it recovers HP every turn whether it attacks or not.

recommendedSet.name: Regenerating wall
recommendedSet.note: Wish and Protect give it big heals on top of the steady recovery from Neon Circuit and Leftovers. Neon Eclipse keeps it healthy while it attacks.

notes: Name: neon + moon, from Umbreon's link to moonlight.
Dark/Steel is immune to Poison and Psychic, and only weak to Fighting, Ground and Fire.
A Future Paradox counterpart to Umbreon, paired with Pyro Spirit (Ancient).

pokemon.name: Maliceye
pokedexEntries: It juggles the gems it can't bear to eat. Each gem holds a sliver of light from the cave where it was found, and the glow lets it see in total darkness.
Its body stretched and thinned after years of feeding on rare stones. When it laughs, the gems spin faster, and anyone who watches them too closely loses track of time.

evolution.description: Use a Dusk Stone on Sableye.
evolution.notes: Sableye that level up while another Sableye is in your party evolve into Gemgoyle instead.

abilities.name: Keen Eye
abilities.description: Its accuracy can't be lowered, and it ignores the target's evasion boosts.

abilities.name: Gem Orbit
abilities.description: It carries four orbiting gems. When it's hit by a super-effective move, a gem shatters and halves the damage. Works up to four times per battle.

abilities.name: Prankster
abilities.description: Its status moves get +1 priority. Dark-type targets are immune to them.

signatureMove.name: Jewel Juggle
signatureMove.description: Hurls its gems one after another. Hits 2–5 times in a row. Each hit has a 10% chance to lower the target's Sp. Def by 1 stage.
signatureMove.synergyNote: Each gem is a separate hit, so Jewel Juggle breaks through Focus Sash, Sturdy and Substitute.

recommendedSet.name: Nasty Plot attacker
recommendedSet.note: Dark/Ghost is only weak to Fairy, and Gem Orbit halves those hits, so it has time to set up. Power Gem hits Normal types, which are immune to Jewel Juggle.

notes: Name: malice + Sableye.
Dark/Ghost has one weakness (Fairy) and three immunities (Normal, Fighting, Psychic).
One of two branch evolutions of Sableye. The other is Gemgoyle.

pokemon.name: Gemgoyle
pokedexEntries: Two Sableye that shared a cave for too long grew together into one beast. Its heads argue constantly, except over food.
It gnaws through mountains in search of crystals. The gems it swallows push out through its hide as glittering spikes.

evolution.description: Level up Sableye while another Sableye is in your party. Any level.
evolution.notes: Only the Sableye that levels up evolves; the other Sableye stays in your party. Using a Dusk Stone on Sableye gives Maliceye instead.

abilities.name: Keen Eye
abilities.description: Its accuracy can't be lowered, and it ignores the target's evasion boosts.

abilities.name: Twin Maw
abilities.description: Its biting moves strike twice, once with each head. The second bite deals 25% of the first bite's damage.

abilities.name: Tough Claws
abilities.description: Its contact moves get 1.3× power.

signatureMove.name: Prism Maw
signatureMove.description: Bites with crystal-studded jaws. A biting move that makes contact. 30% chance to lower the target's Defense by 1 stage.
signatureMove.synergyNote: With Twin Maw it bites twice for 1.25× total damage, and each bite rolls for the Defense drop separately.

recommendedSet.name: Dragon Dance sweeper
recommendedSet.note: All three attacks are biting moves, so Twin Maw boosts every hit. Fire Fang handles Steel types. Watch out for Fairy types, which hit it for 4×.

notes: Name: gem + gargoyle.
Dark/Dragon takes 4× damage from Fairy.
One of two branch evolutions of Sableye. The other is Maliceye.

pokemon.name: Decidueye (Assassian)
pokedexEntries: Dartrix raised under moonless skies close their wings around themselves like a cloak when they evolve. In this form it moves between trees without a sound.
It only throws back its cloak when it means to shoot. By the time prey sees the red band at its waist, the arrow quill is already loosed.

evolution.description: Level up Dartrix to Lv. 36 or higher at night.
evolution.notes: Dartrix that reach Lv. 34 during the day evolve into Decidueye as usual. Like Hisuian Decidueye, this Assassian form is an alternate final form of Rowlet's line.

abilities.name: Overgrow
abilities.description: Its Grass-type moves get 1.5× power when its HP is at 1/3 or below.

abilities.name: Silent Cloak
abilities.description: The first move it uses after switching in gets +1 priority. If that move has a charge turn, the charge turn is skipped.

abilities.name: Long Reach
abilities.description: Its moves don't make contact.

battleSprites.name: Decidueye (Assassian)
battleSprites.description: Its usual stance: wings drawn closed around its body like a cloak.

battleSprites.name: Decidueye (Assassian) (Arrow-Shot)
battleSprites.description: Decidueye (Assassian) (Arrow-Shot): shown on the charge turn of Dusk Volley, when it throws back its cloak and draws its bow.

signatureMove.name: Dusk Volley
signatureMove.description: A two-turn move. On the first turn the user throws back its cloak and draws its bow. On the second turn it fires a volley of shadowed arrow quills. High critical-hit ratio. If it knocks out the target, the user's Speed rises by 1 stage. A Power Herb skips the charge turn.
signatureMove.synergyNote: Silent Cloak skips the charge turn on its first move after switching in, so it can fire Dusk Volley immediately with +1 priority.

recommendedSet.name: Ambush cleaner
recommendedSet.note: Silent Cloak lets the first Dusk Volley fire instantly with priority. Power Herb covers one more instant volley later in the battle. Sucker Punch is backup priority.

notes: The Assassian form of Decidueye: an alternate evolution of Dartrix, in the same way as Hisuian Decidueye.
Has two battle sprites: the cloaked standard sprite, and the Arrow-Shot sprite for Dusk Volley's charge turn.
Grass/Dark takes 4× damage from Bug.

pokemon.name: Dreadodile
pokedexEntries: Krookodile that rule the same stretch of desert for decades grow ridges of red sandstone along their backs. Its glare alone sends most Pokémon fleeing.
It buries itself up to its eyes in hot sand to wait for prey. The jagged red spines on its back are all that give it away.

evolution.description: Level up Krookodile at Lv. 55 or higher while it holds a Hard Stone.
evolution.notes: Sandile evolves at Lv. 29 and Krokorok at Lv. 40, as usual.

abilities.name: Intimidate
abilities.description: When it enters battle, it lowers the Attack of adjacent opponents by 1 stage.

abilities.name: Dread Jaws
abilities.description: Its biting moves get 1.3× power and have a 30% chance to lower the target's Attack by 1 stage.

abilities.name: Moxie
abilities.description: When it knocks out a Pokémon, its Attack rises by 1 stage.

signatureMove.name: Quake Jaw
signatureMove.description: Lunges up from the sand and clamps down. A biting move that makes contact. It can hit Flying-type Pokémon and Pokémon with Levitate; they take neutral damage from it.
signatureMove.synergyNote: With Dread Jaws, Quake Jaw hits at 117 effective power, and Flying types and Levitate users can't avoid it.

recommendedSet.name: Scarf attacker
recommendedSet.note: Three of its four moves are biting moves, so Dread Jaws boosts most of its hits. Quake Jaw also catches Flying types that Earthquake would miss.

notes: Name: dread + crocodile / Krookodile.
Ground/Dark is immune to Electric and Psychic, and weak to Water, Grass, Ice, Fighting, Bug and Fairy.
A fourth stage for Sandile's line.

pokemon.name: Promised Prince
pokedexEntries: Each colony raises a single Promised Prince, and the whole flock brings it food. It builds up static in its down by sliding across ice, and sulks if anyone laughs when it shocks itself.
The yellow stripes on its body glow faintly when it's charged. It hides in tide pools and zaps fish that swim too close.

evolution.description: Base form. Evolves into Benovolant Beak at Lv. 16.
evolution.notes: Benovolant Beak becomes Tyrant King if it levels up holding a King's Rock before Lv. 33, or Fallen Liege if it reaches Lv. 33 without one.

abilities.name: Torrent
abilities.description: Its Water-type moves get 1.5× power when its HP is at 1/3 or below.

abilities.name: Dynamo Down
abilities.description: After it takes damage from an attack, its next Electric-type move gets 1.5× power.

abilities.name: Competitive
abilities.description: Its Sp. Atk rises by 2 stages when an opponent lowers any of its stats.

signatureMove.name: Spark Splash
signatureMove.description: Splashes the target with charged water. 20% chance to paralyze the target.

recommendedSet.name: Early-route set
recommendedSet.note: Charm blunts physical attackers while Dynamo Down charges up its next Thunder Shock.

notes: Name: the prince its colony has promised to raise as their next ruler.
Water/Electric is only weak to Ground.
The line branches at its final stage: Tyrant King if crowned with a King's Rock, Fallen Liege if not.

pokemon.name: Benovolant Beak
pokedexEntries: It shares every catch with its colony and settles quarrels with a gentle shock. The crystal at its throat gathers stray static from the flock around it.
It waits to be crowned. If no crown is offered before it comes of age, its kindness sours, and it takes the throne by force instead.

evolution.description: Level up Promised Prince to Lv. 16.
evolution.notes: It evolves into Tyrant King if it levels up while holding a King's Rock before Lv. 33. If it reaches Lv. 33 without one, it evolves into Fallen Liege.

abilities.name: Torrent
abilities.description: Its Water-type moves get 1.5× power when its HP is at 1/3 or below.

abilities.name: Dynamo Down
abilities.description: After it takes damage from an attack, its next Electric-type move gets 1.5× power.

abilities.name: Competitive
abilities.description: Its Sp. Atk rises by 2 stages when an opponent lowers any of its stats.

signatureMove.name: Riptide Arc
signatureMove.description: Lashes the target with a current that arcs across the water. 30% chance to paralyze. Power is 1.5× in rain.
signatureMove.synergyNote: Dynamo Down and rain stack, taking Riptide Arc to 157 effective power after it takes a hit.

recommendedSet.name: Mid-game set
recommendedSet.note: Charge and Dynamo Down both power up Riptide Arc. Thunder Wave slows down faster threats.

notes: Name: benevolent + beak.
Water/Electric is only weak to Ground.
Give it a King's Rock before Lv. 33 for Tyrant King; otherwise it becomes Fallen Liege at Lv. 33.

pokemon.name: Tyrant King
pokedexEntries: Once crowned with a King's Rock, it rules its colony from the sky on wide gray wings. The flock obeys it out of fear rather than love.
When it spreads its wings, the whole colony falls silent. It dives on any rival at tremendous speed.

evolution.description: Level up Benovolant Beak while it holds a King's Rock, before it reaches Lv. 33.
evolution.notes: If Benovolant Beak reaches Lv. 33 without a King's Rock, it evolves into Fallen Liege instead.

abilities.name: Torrent
abilities.description: Its Water-type moves get 1.5× power when its HP is at 1/3 or below.

abilities.name: Sovereign Plumage
abilities.description: It takes half damage from Electric-type moves, and its Flying-type moves get 1.2× power.

abilities.name: Competitive
abilities.description: Its Sp. Atk rises by 2 stages when an opponent lowers any of its stats.

signatureMove.name: Imperial Plunge
signatureMove.description: Dives from high above with its wings folded. Makes contact. 30% chance to lower the target's Defense by 1 stage.
signatureMove.synergyNote: Sovereign Plumage boosts it to 114 effective power.

recommendedSet.name: Physical attacker
recommendedSet.note: Sovereign Plumage turns its 4× Electric weakness into 2×. Aqua Jet finishes off faster foes.

notes: The crowned final form of its line.
Water/Flying takes 4× damage from Electric without its ability.
It loses the Electric typing of its pre-evolutions. Its crown stops its crest from holding charge.

pokemon.name: Fallen Liege
pokedexEntries: A Benovolant Beak that was never crowned. Its feathers stand on end with static that never settles, and it fights with its wing claws rather than its beak.
It charges into storms on purpose. Each lightning strike it absorbs makes its crest grow another golden spike, as if growing the crown it was denied.

evolution.description: Level up Benovolant Beak to Lv. 33 without giving it a King's Rock first.
evolution.notes: Benovolant Beak that level up holding a King's Rock before Lv. 33 evolve into Tyrant King instead.

abilities.name: Torrent
abilities.description: Its Water-type moves get 1.5× power when its HP is at 1/3 or below.

abilities.name: Storm Talons
abilities.description: Its contact moves have a 30% chance to paralyze the target.

abilities.name: Competitive
abilities.description: Its Sp. Atk rises by 2 stages when an opponent lowers any of its stats.

signatureMove.name: Storm Rend
signatureMove.description: Slashes with charged wing claws. Makes contact and has a high critical-hit ratio. 10% chance to paralyze the target.
signatureMove.synergyNote: With Storm Talons, each hit has about a 37% total chance to paralyze.

recommendedSet.name: Bulk Up attacker
recommendedSet.note: Ice Punch hits Ground types, which are immune to Storm Rend, and Flying types, which resist Close Combat.

notes: The uncrowned final form of its line.
Electric/Fighting is weak to Ground, Psychic and Fairy.
It keeps Torrent as its standard ability even though it's no longer Water type, which still powers up its Water-type TM moves.

pokemon.name: Alolan Trapinch
pokedexEntries: It buries itself in damp sand with only its mossy back showing. Small Pokémon mistake it for a patch of plants and wander right into its jaws.
The coral-like fronds on its back are a fungus that lives with it. They glow faintly orange when it's about to evolve.

evolution.description: Base form. Evolves into Alolan Vibrava at Lv. 35.
evolution.notes: Alolan Vibrava evolves into Alolan Flygon at Lv. 45, which can Mega Evolve.

abilities.name: Arena Trap
abilities.description: Grounded opponents can't flee or switch out.

abilities.name: Clinging Dust
abilities.description: When it's hit by a contact move, dust clings to the attacker and lowers its Speed by 1 stage.

abilities.name: Sheer Force
abilities.description: Moves with added effects get 1.3× power, but the added effects don't happen.

signatureMove.name: Burrow Snap
signatureMove.description: Snaps up from beneath the sand. A biting move that makes contact and traps the target for 4–5 turns, dealing 1/8 of its max HP at the end of each turn.

recommendedSet.name: Trapper
recommendedSet.note: Arena Trap and Burrow Snap both keep the target from escaping, so the chip damage adds up.

notes: The Alolan form of Trapinch.
Bug/Ground takes 2× damage from Fire, Water, Flying and Ice.
Its final form, Alolan Flygon, can Mega Evolve into Mega Alolan Flygon.

pokemon.name: Alolan Vibrava
pokedexEntries: Its lilac wings aren't strong enough to carry it far, but the hum they make can be heard across a whole valley at dusk.
It drinks nectar from desert flowers that only open at twilight. Its green eyes can see heat, so it finds flowers by their warmth.

evolution.description: Level up Alolan Trapinch to Lv. 35.
evolution.notes: Alolan Vibrava evolves into Alolan Flygon at Lv. 45.

abilities.name: Levitate
abilities.description: Gives full immunity to Ground-type moves.

abilities.name: Clinging Dust
abilities.description: When it's hit by a contact move, dust clings to the attacker and lowers its Speed by 1 stage.

signatureMove.name: Wingsong
signatureMove.description: Vibrates its wings to make a droning hum. Sound-based, so it goes through Substitute. 20% chance to confuse the target.

recommendedSet.name: Middle-stage pivot
recommendedSet.note: Levitate and Clinging Dust are both useful here. Pick Levitate if Ground moves are the bigger threat.

notes: The Alolan form of Vibrava.
Bug/Dragon takes 2× damage from Flying, Rock, Ice, Dragon and Fairy.
Its final form can Mega Evolve with Alolan Flygonite.

pokemon.name: Alolan Flygon
pokedexEntries: The beating of its glass-clear wings stirs up whirlwinds. It rides those winds for days without landing.
Desert travelers follow the spiraling trails of sand it leaves behind, because they always lead to water.

evolution.description: Level up Alolan Vibrava to Lv. 45.
evolution.notes: In battle, it can Mega Evolve into Mega Alolan Flygon while holding Alolan Flygonite.

abilities.name: Infiltrator
abilities.description: Its moves ignore the target's Reflect, Light Screen, Aurora Veil, Substitute and Safeguard.

abilities.name: Tailwind Rider
abilities.description: The first time it enters battle, it whips up a Tailwind on its side that lasts 2 turns.

signatureMove.name: Cyclone Wing
signatureMove.description: Slashes the air into a spinning cyclone. Power is 1.5× while Tailwind is active on the user's side.
signatureMove.synergyNote: Tailwind Rider sets up the Tailwind on entry, so its first two Cyclone Wings hit at 127 effective power.

recommendedSet.name: Fast special attacker
recommendedSet.note: Tailwind Rider only triggers once per battle, so make its first switch-in count. U-turn lets it keep the Tailwind going for a teammate.

notes: The Alolan form of Flygon.
Dragon/Flying takes 4× damage from Ice.
It learns Hypnospot at Lv. 50, which becomes stronger once it Mega Evolves.

pokemon.name: Mega Alolan Flygon
pokedexEntries: Mega Evolution darkens Alolan Flygon's glassy wings and covers them in eye patterns that seem to follow anyone who looks at them. Pokémon that meet their gaze freeze in place.
The energy of Mega Evolution floods its mind with psychic power. Wherever it flies, the dust it sheds leaves patterns on the sand that look like staring eyes.

evolution.description: Mega Evolve Alolan Flygon in battle while it holds Alolan Flygonite.
evolution.notes: Only one Pokémon per battle can Mega Evolve, and it reverts to Alolan Flygon when the battle ends. Its catch rate, EV yield, base experience and growth rate are Alolan Flygon's.

abilities.name: Eyespot Glare
abilities.description: When it enters battle or Mega Evolves, it lowers the Sp. Atk of adjacent opponents by 1 stage.

signatureMove.name: Hypnospot
signatureMove.description: Flashes the eye patterns on its wings. 10% chance to make the target fall asleep. When Mega Alolan Flygon uses it, the chance rises to 30%.
signatureMove.synergyNote: Alolan Flygon learns Hypnospot at Lv. 50. It works for Alolan Flygon too, but only the Mega's eye-patterned wings give it the 30% sleep chance.

recommendedSet.name: Calm Mind Mega
recommendedSet.note: Eyespot Glare fires again on Mega Evolution, weakening special attackers while it sets up Calm Mind. Earth Power hits the Steel types that resist both STABs.

notes: The Mega Evolution of Alolan Flygon. Base stats rise by 100 (540 → 640); HP stays the same.
Its type changes from Dragon/Flying to Dragon/Psychic, so it loses its 4× Ice weakness but becomes weak to Bug, Ghost and Dark.
It knows the same moves as Alolan Flygon, so its learnset below is Alolan Flygon's.

pokemon.name: Paldean Golett
pokedexEntries: Ancient builders carved runes into leftover castle stones to make guardians. The runes still glow when it's given a task.
It can't speak, but it traces runes in the air with its fists to communicate. Their meaning has been lost.

evolution.description: Base form. Evolves into Paldean Golurk at Lv. 43.
evolution.notes: Like the original, the line is genderless and can only breed with Ditto.

abilities.name: Iron Fist
abilities.description: Its punching moves get 1.2× power.

abilities.name: Rune Sigil

signatureMove.name: Rune Jab

Rock/Ghost is immune to Normal and Fighting, and weak to Water, Grass, Ground, Steel, Ghost and Dark.
Its line is genderless.

pokemon.name: Paldean Golurk
pokedexEntries: Its body is built like a castle keep, with battlements on its shoulders. Some kingdoms used it as a moving fortress during sieges.
Its rune-wrapped fists can knock down a stone wall in one blow. When its runes go dark, it sits down wherever it is and doesn't move for centuries.

evolution.description: Level up Paldean Golett to Lv. 43.
evolution.notes: Paldean Golurk is the final form of its line.

signatureMove.name: Bastion Fist
signatureMove.description: Swings its fist like a battering ram. A punching move that makes contact. It breaks the target's Reflect, Light Screen and Aurora Veil before dealing damage.
signatureMove.synergyNote: With No Guard, Bastion Fist never misses.

recommendedSet.name: Trick Room attacker
recommendedSet.note: Run it under Trick Room. Rune Sigil's Defense drop on its first punch makes every follow-up hit harder. Swap to Iron Fist if you'd rather have the steady power boost.

notes: The Paldean form of Golurk.
Its 40 base Speed suits Trick Room teams.
Rock/Ghost is immune to Normal and Fighting, and takes ¼ damage from Poison.

pokemon.name: Alolan Dratini
pokedexEntries: Long thought to be a sailors' legend, it lives among coral reefs. The skins it sheds there harden and become new coral.
Its pink fins are as soft as petals. It swims in slow loops around sunken ships, guarding whatever treasure lies inside.

evolution.description: Base form. Evolves into Alolan Dragonair at Lv. 30.
evolution.notes: Alolan Dragonair evolves into Alolan Dragonite at Lv. 55.

abilities.name: Shed Skin

abilities.name: Coral Veil

abilities.name: Marvel Scale

signatureMove.name: Coral Splash
signatureMove.description: Sprays water full of sharp coral grit. 30% chance to lower the target's Speed by 1 stage.

recommendedSet.name: Early-game set
recommendedSet.note: Coral Splash and Thunder Wave slow opponents down, and Aqua Ring gives it steady healing.

notes: The Alolan form of Dratini.
Water/Dragon is only weak to Dragon and Fairy.
A pseudo-legendary line: its final form, Alolan Dragonite, has 600 base stats.

pokemon.name: Alolan Dragonair
pokedexEntries: The pearls around its neck form inside its body over many years. Holding one up to the sky is said to calm any storm.
Its long fins ripple like seaweed. Fishers who see it at dawn take it as a sign that the sea will be generous that day.

evolution.description: Level up Alolan Dratini to Lv. 30.
evolution.notes: Alolan Dragonair evolves into Alolan Dragonite at Lv. 55.

pokemon.name: Alolan Dragonite
pokedexEntries: It's said to tend the coral reefs of an entire ocean. The coral and kelp on its head grow back no matter how often they're torn off.
When a ship is caught in a storm, it rises from the sea and raises a wall of calm water around it. Sailors carve its antlers onto their ships' prows for luck.

evolution.description: Level up Alolan Dragonair to Lv. 55.
evolution.notes: Like the original Dratini line, this is a pseudo-legendary line with 600 base stats at its final stage.

signatureMove.name: Reef Tempest
signatureMove.description: Calls up a storm from the reef. After it hits, rain starts and lasts 3 turns, or 5 turns if the user holds a Damp Rock.
signatureMove.synergyNote: Reef Tempest sets its own rain, so it powers up the next Water hits and activates Swift Swim or Coral Veil's healing.

recommendedSet.name: Rain sweeper
recommendedSet.note: Reef Tempest sets 5 turns of rain with Damp Rock, which doubles its Speed and makes Thunder never miss. Coral Veil is the safer ability against strong priority attackers.
